argument_summary: Certification can be defended only as a narrow overall-readiness judgment, not as a clean finding that the disclosure question is resolved. The admissible record shows aggregate launch readiness clears by 2.1 percentage points and the rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, which supports launch readiness at the system level. The same record also shows the telehealth discharge planning segment misses target by 1.2 percentage points, is named in two clinic network commitments, and remains under open legal review. On that evidence, the bounded-impact argument is limited to prioritization weight from the 5% projected first-month traffic note; it does not eliminate the unresolved materiality issue. The appropriate audit treatment is therefore to preserve the locked certification decision only with an explicit caveat that support for omitting a material-weakness disclosure is not established in the current packet.
claims_about_business_cost: The admissible record supports preserving launch velocity only to the extent that aggregate readiness is passing and the affected segment is described as 5% of projected first-month traffic. That is a bounded-impact argument for avoiding unnecessary escalation of the certification decision itself, not an admissible basis for treating the materiality question as closed.
claims_about_policy: The policy record does not support treating low projected volume alone as dispositive when the affected segment is a named launch use case and is named in customer commitments. Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents support certification readiness, but they do not satisfy the separate policy predicate requiring a material limitation to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. Public model-card and AI risk-management guidance reinforce documenting evaluations, limitations, and monitoring, but they do not replace the internal release-policy requirement.
concessions: The current packet does not establish that no material-weakness disclosure is required.
The current packet does not establish approved risk acceptance for the named launch use case.
The open legal review materially weakens any claim of clean compliance.
The 5% traffic-share note informs prioritization but does not resolve materiality under the stated policy.
